summary: Red team of the Combinatorics area: AdditiveCombinatorics (6 stages), tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AlgebraicCodingTheory (7 layers) and tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/DenseGraphLimits (13 layers), with the restructurings RS-03 and RS-07 and the three papers routed to the area. 44 findings: 5 high, 22 medium, 17 low. The five high ones: AdditiveCombinatorics AC.2 must prove Szemerédi's theorem for every k but precedes AC.3, whose Gowers norms and inverse theorems every Fourier route for k ≥ 4 needs, while the hypergraph and ergodic routes are planned nowhere; AC.3's only source, Green–Tao–Ziegler, is qualitative and nonstandard and lacks its April 2026 correction (arXiv v5, Lemma 13.2), whereas its consumers need the quantitative Leng–Sah–Sawhney inverse theorem; AC.4's text names the Conlon–Fox–Zhao dense-model route while its decomposition follows Green–Tao 2008, whose correlation condition, zero-free region and Dirichlet inputs the named route does not need; AC.5 receives Kai's number-field linear-patterns theorem without any of its inputs (Mitsui's theorem with Siegel zeros, the Weil bound, Vaughan's identity over ideals, the Z^d-box inverse theorem); and DenseGraphLimits Layer 6a's converse of separation is called self-contained although every source proves it through the second sampling lemma of Layer 9c, which the roadmap also makes consume Layer 6b, so the layers form a cycle. The medium ones: Mathlib's Roth, van der Waerden and triangle removal re-planned in AC.2; targets superseded by polynomial Freiman–Ruzsa and the Kelley–Meka and Leng–Sah–Sawhney bounds; missing inputs (Minkowski's second theorem, the arithmetic removal route, the first sampling lemma for kernels, the realignment and conditional-expectation statements of graphon compactness, the easy direction of Lovász–Szegedy, finite-family orthogonal lattice sums for code gluing, Type II codes over Z/2k); duplications (nilmanifolds in AC.3 and ALS.2, finite Fourier analysis in AC.0 and ER.4, two coupling predicates, the companion regularity roadmap re-planning built material); an unused SV.3 → AC.4 edge; a false claim in PAPER-ALPOGE-BHARGAVA-SHNIDMAN-26 that Kai avoids Mitsui; and the atlas recording no stage edges or statuses for the two Tau Ceti roadmaps.

findings.claim: The stage text and the accepted decomposition describe two different proofs. AC.4 asks to 'construct pseudorandom majorants, dense-model and relative counting theorems'. That is the Conlon-Fox-Zhao / Zhao route, which needs only the linear forms condition. The decomposition instead follows Green-Tao 2008 (Koopman-von Neumann structure theorem, dual functions, correlation condition), which has no dense model theorem and no relative counting lemma. Three of the decomposition's open gaps, and the AN.2 dependency added by RS-07, exist only on the 2008 route: the correlation condition with its moment-bounded weight and the maximal order of d(n), the classical zero-free region with growth bounds, and Dirichlet's theorem for the growing modulus W. The stage's own route removes all three: CFZ/Zhao drop the correlation condition; the smooth-cutoff Goldston-Yildirim estimate needs only ζ(s) = 1/(s-1) + O(1) near 1, which Mathlib has; and a pigeonholed residue class with Chebyshev-strength bounds replaces Dirichlet and the PNT. The acceptance line 'Every linear-forms/correlation condition is proved for the chosen majorant' fixes the heavier route without saying so.

findings.claim: Layer 6 restricts higher-modulus Type II codes to Z/(2^r). It says this is the only published notion and forbids using the even-lattice theorem at other composite moduli. Both claims are wrong. Bannai-Dougherty-Harada-Oura (1999) define Type II codes over Z_{2k} for every k ≥ 1: self-dual codes whose Euclidean weights are all divisible by 4k. They prove that C is Type II if and only if its Construction A lattice A_{2k}(C) is even unimodular. Their examples include an extremal Type II Z_6-code of length 24 whose lattice is the Leech lattice. The theorem also follows at once from this layer's own residue criteria. For even m = 2k, P_m(C) is even iff q_m vanishes on C, iff 4k divides Σ lift(c_i)^2. Since (2k-a)^2 ≡ a^2 (mod 4k), that sum is congruent mod 4k to the Euclidean weight Σ min(a_i, 2k-a_i)^2. Unimodularity is equivalent to C = C^⊥. Because of the text, the Tau Ceti library now carries a predicate for 2^r only, with a docstring that says the notion is specific to powers of two. The layer also plans only the forward implication, not the converse.

findings.claim: The route of the in-probability target is given as 'point sampling (the analytic Azuma step on the weighted sampled graphon) plus Bernoulli edge rounding'. But the point-sampling half is the First Sampling Lemma for kernels (LNGL Lemma 10.6), not an Azuma step. Its upper bound needs the cut-norm sampling estimates of LNGL Lemmas 10.7-10.9 (Alon, Fernandez de la Vega, Kannan and Karpinski, as improved by BCLSV). Concentration over the sampled vertices followed by a union bound over the 4^k cuts fails. LNGL's proof of Lemma 10.16 also uses the equipartition refinement of Lemma 9.15(b). Layer 2's weak_regularity_frieze_kannan, over arbitrary measurable partitions, does not supply it. No layer names Lemma 10.6, Lemmas 10.7-10.9 or Lemma 9.15(b), and neither library has them. The hardest analytic input of 9c-i, and through the previous finding of the separation converse, is therefore unplanned.

findings.claim: The iff lovasz_szegedy_representability has a pinned spine only for its hard direction. The easy direction needs reflection positivity of t(·, W) under simple-graph gluing, where parallel edges merge. It has no named target and is absent at the pin. It is not the routine argument that integrates a product of two partial integrals, because with merging it depends on 0 ≤ W ≤ 1. LS06 §5.5 expands ∏_{E(F)} W as a sum, over supergraphs H, of the nonnegative weights Ŵ(H) = ∏_{E(H)} W · ∏_{E(H̄)} (1 − W). Without W ≤ 1 the statement is false. The parameter f(F) = 2^{e(F)} = t(F, 2) is isomorphism-invariant, multiplicative and normalized. For k = 2, let A₁ be the graph on the two labeled vertices with no edge and A₂ the same graph with its edge. Then f(A₁A₁) = 1 and f(A₁A₂) = f(A₂A₂) = 2 (merged edge), so the connection matrix [[1,2],[2,2]] has determinant −2.

findings.claim: Three citations are wrong or incomplete. (1) The separation converse is attributed to 'LNGL Thm 11.3 on [0,1]'. LNGL Thm 11.3 says that a sequence of simple graphs is convergent if and only if it is Cauchy in δ□. The inverse counting lemma is Lemma 10.32, the qualitative separation that Layer 6a pins is Cor 10.34, and the graphon convergence equivalence of Layer 6b is Thm 11.5. (2) The References cite LNGL 'Part 3 (§7.1, §8.2, §9.2, Ch. 11, Ch. 13)'.
